Copy the validation kit: templates to validate rtfreporter in your environment

Source: R/validation_kit.R
rtfreporter_validation_kit.Rd

rtfreporter ships its own quality records – the Functional Requirements (FR), the tests mapped to them and, at each release, a Quality Report. Your company still has to show that the package is fit for its use in its environment. This copies the templates for that into a folder, to edit and fill:

Usage

rtfreporter_validation_kit(dir, overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

dir

The folder to write into. Created if it does not exist.

overwrite

FALSE (default) refuses a folder that already has files in it; TRUE writes into it, replacing the kit's files of the same name.

Value

The paths of the files written, invisibly.

Details

validation_plan.md

The Validation Plan: purpose, scope and intended use, roles, the risk-based approach (what the package's evidence covers, what you check), acceptance criteria, deviations.

urs.csv, urs.md

The User Requirement Specification: your needs (UR-NNN), each linked to the package's FR ids; urs.md explains the columns of this file and of the UAT cases.

uat_cases.csv, uat_cases.xlsx

User acceptance test cases (UAT-NNN) on dummy data, with blank actual, result, tester and date to fill.

build_user_matrix.R

Writes your Traceability Matrix (URS -> FR -> UAT): user_traceability_matrix.csv, and user_traceability_matrix.xlsx when writexl is installed.

validation_summary_report.md

The Validation Summary Report you fill: environment, UAT results, deviations, conclusion.

quality-plan.md, requirements.csv

The package's own Quality Plan and Functional Requirements, for reference.

The example content is fictional (a company "Example Pharma"); replace it with your own.

From 0.9.0 on, the package's Quality Report is attached to each GitHub release of rtfreporter as quality-report-<tag>.pdf. It states the results (overall and by area, with the reason for each skipped test), the environments the tests ran on and how they stand for the environments the package supports, the deviations, and the conclusion. Use the report of the release you install: a report from a CI run started by hand is marked DRAFT and concludes nothing. The same release carries the evidence, each file's name ending in the tag: traceability_matrix-<tag>.xlsx (which tests check each requirement), environments-<tag>.txt (every environment's sessionInfo and test log), test-log-<tag>.txt (the mapped tests' log) and the tables behind the results, ft-<tag>.csv, functions-<tag>.csv and candidates-<tag>.csv.

See also

The article "Validating rtfreporter in your environment", https://ichirio.github.io/rtfreporter/articles/validation.html.

Examples

kit <- rtfreporter_validation_kit(file.path(tempdir(), "rtfreporter-validation"))
basename(kit)
#> [1] "build_user_matrix.R"          "uat_cases.csv"               
#> [3] "uat_cases.xlsx"               "urs.csv"                     
#> [5] "urs.md"                       "validation_plan.md"          
#> [7] "validation_summary_report.md" "quality-plan.md"             
#> [9] "requirements.csv"            
unlink(dirname(kit[1]), recursive = TRUE)
